section: finalchorus_love (162.81-192.34 s, bars 88-103, lyric lines 105-127 zero-based = storyboard numbers 106-128)
summary: The section is two 8-bar halves built by two different files: 162.81-177.57 is the "undelivered" twin of chorus 1 (shots cx-give ... cx-trap, produced by src/scenes/05_chorus.js called with CHORUS_X, NOT by 12_outro.js), and 177.57-192.34 is the outro (out-study, out-answers, out-heart, out-frame in src/scenes/12_outro.js). Both halves stay entirely inside the chat client: half one replays chorus 1's seven set-ups with the user's replies replaced by empty dashed outlines and every one of her bubbles stamped with a small red "Reached no one" badge; half two has the AI close fifteen error cards one by one while the palette blends from 'error' red to 'ash' grey, with four LO-O-OVE words set as modest serif headlines inside the page. Musically this is a flat-out plateau: per-bar RMS 0.57-0.64 and high band 0.58-0.75 for all 64 beats (equal to chorus 1, far above EXECUTION's 0.49 / 0.32), stepping up at 162.81 and falling off a cliff only at 192.34. Measured on one frame per beat, the picture is the darkest and least saturated half-minute since the boot: mean luma 41/255 against 75 (chorus 1) and 63 (EXECUTION); bright saturated pixels 2.9 % (cx) and 4.5 % (out) against 13 % and 17 %. No flash, shake, zoom kick, glitch or datamosh is used anywhere in the section, and all four outro cuts are dissolves. The only frame with peak-level light is cx-kw3 (172.73-173.88).

diagnosis:
What the frames show is a deliberate anticlimax laid over the loudest sustained music of the song. The code says so in plain words: 05_chorus.js header "Nothing is re-randomised per frame; nothing pulses with the beat", damage() "no bloom to speak of" (fx.glow = 0.14), and `hit = bad ? {type:'cut'} : {type:'cut', flash:0.3}` (line 490) removes the keyword flashes chorus 1 had; 12_outro.js blends the palette from 'error' to 'ash' in fifteen steps (cool(t), lines 78-82) and uses a dissolve for every cut. The story logic is sound (nothing is delivered; then the errors are calmly dismissed), but the director is reacting to the result on screen:

1. Energy runs the wrong way. Audio per bar is RMS 0.57-0.64, mid 0.68-0.77, high 0.58-0.75 from 162.81 to 192.34 with no thinning (section means: chorus X 0.609 / outro 0.595, against EXECUTION 0.489 and chorus 1 0.613). The picture measures mean luma 41 against 75 in chorus 1 and 63 in EXECUTION; bright saturated pixels 2.9 % and 4.5 % against 13 % and 17 %. In the outro the palette is 22 % ash at LO-O-OVE #1, 60 % at #2, 88 % at #3 and 100 % at #4, so each hit is drawn duller than the one before, and the final one in #b5765d with bloom at about half. The visual decrescendo ends exactly where the music is still at full level; the real drop is at 192.34.

2. Nothing punctuates. In the whole section there are zero flashes, zero shakes, zero zoom kicks, and fx.glitch / fx.mosh are never set (they exist only in 10_error.js bars 73-79). The corrupted chorus's "damage" is a 12 fps time quantisation, a 2.5 px RGB split and a red outline offset by a few pixels: all invisible at viewing size, so the frames look clean, not broken. The outro has no damage at all. The infinite-loop failure of 148-162 therefore does not carry over, which is exactly what the director asks for.

3. The keyword hits are small. LO-O-OVE occupies 37 %, 26 % (x6), 35 % and 48 % of frame width with cap heights of about 100, 77, 90 and 134 px at 1080p, always as one element among sidebar, composer, error cards and an illustration. The EXECUTION words are larger (73 %) but sit in a dark box on a flat dark page. The stutter is not shown: the string is typeset once with hyphens and its glyphs land at an even 0.03-0.045 s step, not on three syllables; nothing repeats, tears or freezes.

4. The subject of most shots is micro-interface. The carrying information is 15-38 px badges, 'Sending…' labels, 20-25 px error-card copy and empty dashed outlines; it reads on a paused frame, not at speed. Several stretches are near-empty or static: the chorus entry at 162.83 (luma 27.6, two small bubbles), 166.50-167.42 (one 50 px bubble plus an empty outline), 175.5-177.1 (a window at zoom 0.84 with only a blinking caret, 3.5 beats under the held note), and all of out-study.

5. Low contrast and a quiet palette by construction: page #1d1413, orange text #d97757 on it, red only as thin lines and small dots, cream almost absent because the user is gone, bloom throttled. The 'error' state here means "matte dark red-brown", unlike EXECUTION's full-field errRed / errCream cards.

6. The illustrations are the wrong style and, in two shots, the wrong hierarchy: the full-colour anime 'library' picture (534x801) and 'parted' figure (580x870) are untreated and are the brightest things in out-study and out-frame (they account for most of those shots' measured brightness), so the eye goes to a picture that clashes with the flat UI rather than to the word. cx-happy and cx-trap use anime art as halftone ('tea', 'gaze').

7. The twin concept makes the peak a weaker repeat: every cx set-up is chorus 1's layout with things removed (no cream replies, no cursor, no flash, no glow), so a viewer sees familiar compositions with less in them at the moment the song asks for more.

Strong and worth keeping: cx-kw3 proves the system can deliver a peak frame (luma 81); the heart drawn from the true implicit curve, traced point by point with live coordinates, is original and literal to the lyric; "every question gets the same word" plus the tally line is the best idea in the section; the misregistered two-plate halftone and the self-pressing retry are good damage vocabulary; the withdrawn request and the user's lane sliding away close the plot. Weak: scale, light, punctuation, corruption, the stutter, the art, and the placement of the calm resolution 15 s too early.
keep: The algebraic heart: algebraicHeart() in src\scenes\12_outro.js lines 32-51 solves (x^2+y^2-1)^3 - x^2 y^3 = 0 by bisection and returns 240 evenly spaced points; out-heart traces it point by point with a pen dot, projection lines, live x/y read-out and 'point n of 240', then fills it with rising cross-hatch (hatch(), line 54). Keep the curve and the tracing, but let it own the frame (it is only about 620x560 px now) and let it be the light source of its hit.

The same-word answers (out-answers): six of the user's old questions taken from the sidebar, one per beat (181.04 ... 183.34), all answered with the one word, and the mono tally 'answers: 6, distinct: 1'. Keep the idea; it is the natural carrier for the stutter and for repetition/loop corruption, at a much larger scale (type.js wall() / sliced() exist for this).

The cx-kw3 lighting recipe (05_chorus.js setup6, lines 415-425): page() with hot:1 and grey:false, spark() of radius 500 filling petal by petal (lit: prog), ctx.glow('me', size*0.16) on the word, fx.glow capped at 0.42. It is the only frame at peak brightness (luma 81, 13-17 % saturated) and shows the level the whole section needs.

The keyword twin logic: EXECUTION sits in the same slot and size as chorus 1's keyword, now inside a red outline (keyword(), 05_chorus.js lines 190-206). The 'same place, now broken' reading is worth keeping even if the bubble box goes.

The 'Reached no one' / 'Tell them again' badge with the retry pill pressing itself with no cursor on screen (badge(), 05_chorus.js lines 142-162; copy in docs/v3/errors.json undelivered). Good story device; keep as an accent, not as the subject of seven shots.

The misregistered two-plate halftone of the picture message (05_chorus.js lines 388-389: grey/dark plate plus a red plate offset 5/3 px). The technique suits the new flat three-ink silhouettes better than the anime art and reads as print damage.
Dropped-frame time: q() (05_chorus.js line 48) samples motion 12 times a second from each cut. Cheap, deterministic, flash-safe; keep and make it visible (lower rate, freeze/repeat on the stutter).

The plot closures in out-frame: the request code block struck through and withdrawn on the 'free' line (request(), 12_outro.js lines 215-231), the user's lane labelled 'Closed by you' sliding out of frame (189.92-190.50), and the second outline sealing the window on 'trapped in' (190.50-191.31). Keep the meaning; restage with the silhouette art.

Errors closing themselves and folding into the component they reddened (pile()/card(), 12_outro.js lines 97-142; CL times line 78). Keep the idea of red leaving, but it is a wind-down device: it belongs after the last hit or in the shutdown, not spread across the 15 loudest seconds.
slam() with its `times[]` argument (src/engine/type.js line 36): per-glyph hit times are already supported, so [lyric] can be struck on three separate syllable times without new engine work.

Colour semantics (orange = me, cream = you, red = error, grey = absence), cuts on the beat grid, lyric text from text(i), and the fact that every lyric line 105-127 is covered and readable for its sung length.
problems: Scene-file pointer is incomplete: 162.81-177.57 (cx-*) is produced by src/scenes/05_chorus.js through the shared factory chorusShots(env, CHORUS_X) (index.js lines 14 and 30). Editing a set-up there also edits chorus 1 unless the change is behind the `bad` switch; a real redesign should fork the corrupted chorus into its own file.

Visual energy is inverse to the music: mean frame luma 41/255 for both halves against 75 (chorus 1) and 63 (EXECUTION); bright saturated pixels 2.9 % / 4.5 % against 13 % / 17 %. Per-beat luma is 27-37 for most of 162.8-170.2, 30-36 for 173.9-177.1, 28-37 for 181.3-188.2.

The outro palette fades to ash while the music stays at full level: cool(t) is 0.22 at LO-O-OVE #1, 0.60 at #2, 0.88 at #3, 1.00 at #4 (ash: me #b5765d, bloom glow 0.6, art sat 0.3). The climax word is the dullest of the four.

No punctuation on any hit: no flash (cx cuts are flash-less by the `bad` switch; outro cuts are dissolves), no shake, no zoom kick, no beat-reactive light. Chorus 1 had flash 0.3-0.35 on its hits; the final chorus has none.

No visible corruption: fx.glitch and fx.mosh are 0 for the whole section; fx.rgbSplit is 2.5 px (1.5 in cx-happy) and only in the cx half; the outro has no damage at all. Transition types glitch / slices / shatter / flashcut exist in src/engine/transitions.js and are unused here.

All four outro transitions are dissolves (2 beats, then 1 beat each, three of them starting ON the cut), so each LO-O-OVE is cross-faded away 1.6-2.0 beats after it lands and no outro cut has an edge.

LO-O-OVE is small: 705 px (37 % of width), 6 x 500 px (26 %), 665 px (35 %), 930 px (48 %); cap heights about 100 / 77 / 90 / 134 px. In every case it shares the frame with a sidebar or figure, a composer, an error-card pile and small lyric lines.
The stutter is not visualised: the word is one typeset string; glyphs land at an even 0.03-0.045 s step within 0.24-0.36 s; no repeat, hold, tear or re-trigger on the three syllables.

The chorus entry has no impact: at 162.81 the music steps from RMS 0.44 / high 0.27 (bar 87) to 0.57 / 0.73, and the picture hard-cuts without flash to an almost empty dark window corner with two bubbles of 30-40 px type.

Micro-UI as subject: 15-38 px badges, 'Sending…', retry pills, 14 px mono header note, 520x164 error cards with 20-25 px copy changing 15 times, 22 px coordinate read-outs. The narrative is readable only on a paused frame.

Empty dashed outlines carry the 'nobody answers' idea in five of seven cx shots; they are thin 2-3 px grey dashes on dark brown and leave 50-70 % of the frame as flat dark page (cx-only first two beats: luma std 5.7).
Static stretches under loud music: 175.5-177.1 (window at zoom 0.84, only a caret blinks, 3.5 beats, luma 30); out-study 177.57-179.88 (static layout, two 44 px lines typing); out-frame after 191.81.

Low contrast: orange #d97757 text and 2-5 px red lines on #1d1413 / #2d1c1a surfaces; cream (the film's brightest ink) nearly absent; bloom throttled to 0.14 in six of seven cx shots and x0.6 in out-study.

Illustration uses, all anime style and all to be replaced: (1) 'tea' as halftone picture message 667x1000 to 736x1104 in cx-happy; (2) 'tea' halftone thumbnail 100x150 in cx-trap; (3) 'gaze' halftone figure 700x1050 behind the page in cx-trap; (4) 'library' untreated 534x801 in out-study; (5) 'parted' untreated full figure 580x870 in out-frame, continued in 13_shutdown.js lines 54 and 60; (6) blurred backdrops: 'tea' in every cx shot (alpha 0.1-0.2) and 'library' in out-study / out-answers (alpha 0.35-0.4).

In out-study and out-frame the untreated anime picture is the brightest and most saturated object and out-ranks the keyword (those two shots' luma of 50-56 comes mostly from the cream dress, not from designed graphics).
The chorus-twin structure shows chorus 1's compositions a second time with elements removed; at the peak of the song the viewer gets less than at 59-74 s.
The error-card pile adds a second reading task in three of four outro shots and keeps a busy red object in a corner while the word should hold the frame.

New-art facts a designer must plan for: the four female silhouettes in 圖片/Claude娘剪影 are BUSTS (1254x1254 and 1086x1448/1449), not full figures, so out-frame's 'standing whole inside the frame' and the shutdown handover rect cannot be reused as is; their black ink is the same value as the page background (#1d1413 / #1c1b1a), so on the current dark page a third of the shapes would vanish (they need a lighter or saturated field, e.g. the errCream / errRed / orange plates); the cut-out edges carry stray red/orange fringe pixels that will show on dark grounds and in art.silhouette(). Poses: -1 three-quarter face with one visible glaring eye; -2 eyes closed, one hand at the chest, the other reaching toward the viewer; -3 profile facing left, eyes hidden by the fringe; -4 frontal with the face entirely black.
Minor: pickup lines start before their shot's cut (line 105 at 162.63, cut 162.81; line 116 at 177.25, cut 177.57), so their first 0.2-0.3 s falls in the previous shot or inside a dissolve.
